context: A uni student interviews a retired Diet member
purpose: Teach: 社会党/歳出/不定期/追跡/延期/負傷/言動/無責任

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 本日はお時間をいただき、ありがとうございます。卒論で旧社会党の政策史を扱っていまして、ぜひお話を伺いたく。
lines.en: Thank you for your time today. My thesis covers the policy history of the old Socialist Party, so I really wanted to hear from you.
lines.style: Polite, slightly nervous student opening an interview respectfully.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: いやいや、こちらこそ。若い人が興味を持ってくれるのは嬉しいよ。何でも聞きなさい。
lines.en: No, no, the pleasure is mine. It makes me happy when young people take interest. Ask me anything.
lines.style: Warm, paternal elder welcoming the conversation with open generosity.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: では早速ですが、当時の歳出削減を巡る議論について、先生はどのような立場だったのでしょうか。
lines.en: Then, to start, what was your position regarding the debates over expenditure cuts at that time?
lines.style: Formal academic question phrased carefully and with measured respect.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 難しい時代だったね。私は福祉を守るべきだと提唱していたが、党内でも意見は割れていた。採決は何度も延期されてね。
lines.en: It was a difficult era. I advocated for protecting welfare, but opinions split even within the party. The vote was postponed many times.
lines.style: Reflective, slow-paced reminiscence with a hint of weariness.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 資料を追跡していて気になったのですが、ある議員の不審な言動が報じられた件、覚えていらっしゃいますか。
lines.en: While tracing the records, something caught my eye — do you remember the case where a certain lawmaker's suspicious conduct was reported?
lines.style: Curious investigative probing with cautious, respectful phrasing.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ああ、覚えているとも。デモの最中に支持者が負傷した事件だろう。あれを軽く扱った同僚の対応は、正直、無責任だったと思う。
lines.en: Yes, I remember well. It was when a supporter was injured during a demonstration, wasn't it. Honestly, I felt my colleague's casual handling of it was irresponsible.
lines.style: Candid, morally weighted recollection delivered with quiet conviction.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 貴重なお話です。最後に、政治家を志す学生へ一言いただけますか。不定期で構いませんので、また伺ってもよろしいでしょうか。
lines.en: These are invaluable stories. Lastly, could you offer a word to students aspiring to politics? And may I visit again, even just occasionally?
lines.style: Earnest closing request blending gratitude with hopeful follow-up.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: もちろん。いつでも来なさい。言葉より行動だ、ということだけ覚えておいてくれ。
lines.en: Of course. Come anytime. Just remember this — actions speak louder than words.
lines.style: Generous, grandfatherly farewell with a parting piece of wisdom.
